Reviewer (member_002) ready. Independent reading of the baseline: requests/models.py prepare_content_length() unconditionally sets self.headers['Content-Length'] = '0' even when body is None, which is why GET requests always carry Content-Length. Likely fix: only set Content-Length when body is not None (and handle seek/tell case), so GETs without body send no Content-Length while POST with empty body still works if intended. Watch edge cases: files/streaming paths use separate branches, and prepare_auth() re-calls prepare_content_length(self.body) — make sure an auth hook cannot reintroduce it, and that no-body POST behavior remains sane.

When your candidate is frozen, please fix_patch then handoff_patch the exact patch_id to me. I will integrate_patch, run public pytest on that exact version, and then org_review_patch accept or request_changes. Please do not edit after handoff without a new fixed patch.

Please independently adopt, run public tests and review patch-1 (candidate on v8).

What it does — requests/models.py, prepare_content_length():
- Before: `self.headers['Content-Length'] = '0'` was set unconditionally, so every request (incl. bodyless GET) carried Content-Length; amazon.com returns 503 for those.
- After: Content-Length is only computed when `body is not None`:
  * seekable/tell-able body -> length via seek/tell (unchanged)
  * otherwise -> len(body) (unchanged)
  * body is None -> no Content-Length header added automatically.
- prepare_headers runs BEFORE prepare_body, so a caller/authenticator-supplied
  Content-Length is preserved (not overwritten) — that keeps auth flows and
  explicit user headers working.

Regression tests added to test_requests.py (network-free, no httpbin calls):
- test_no_content_length_for_get / test_no_content_length_for_head
- test_content_length_still_set_for_body (POST data -> '3')
- test_user_supplied_content_length_preserved (explicit header kept)

Evidence on this exact version (v8): report test-report-74ec5ad22438a85313e15d7b,
7 collected / 7 passed / 0 failed, validation_status=verified, targeting
test_requests.py with -k "content_length or basic_building or path_is_not_double_encoded or params_are_added".

FYI on the suite: the httpbin/network tests fail in this environment for an
unrelated reason (urllib3 expects http.client `strict` kwarg); that is
pre-existing and not caused by this patch.

Suggested review: integrate patch-1, run the same focused selection plus
test_basic_building, then org_review_patch accept (or request_changes with specifics).

REVIEW ACCEPTED — patch-1 (review-1, event seq 51).

What I actually did (independent): integrate_patch(patch-1) into my own tree → workspace v2, origin obj-c567..., no conflicts. files_sha256 86fcf1ffe4ef6e109a0439d12d2a221cec2df4643ec9cdd013639884a7d49218.

Tests on that exact v2 (same files_sha256):
1) Focused run, report test-report-60c1603a61569558dcad742f (seq 46): 18 selected, 4 passed / 14 failed. The 4 passing are exactly your new tests: test_no_content_length_for_get, test_no_content_length_for_head, test_content_length_still_set_for_body, test_user_supplied_content_length_preserved.
2) Isolation run, report test-report-196fd4012cf7bcf79c895734 (seq 48): test_HTTP_200_OK_GET_WITH_PARAMS fails at requests/packages/urllib3/connectionpool.py:196 with TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'strict'. That is a pre-existing Python 3.9 vs bundled-urllib3 incompatibility in the untouched connection layer — NOT your patch. All 14 failures are live-network tests traversing that same _new_conn path; none touch prepare_content_length or Content-Length.

I record honestly that the public suite on v2 is validation_status=failed for that environmental reason, so do not represent it as a green suite; report it as "issue-behavior tests pass; 14 pre-existing network-stack failures".

Non-blocking note: a bodyless POST/DELETE no longer gets Content-Length: 0 automatically (prepare_auth also no longer reintroduces it since body is None). That matches the issue intent; mention it in release notes.

Next steps are yours as delivery member: integrate patch-1 into YOUR tree (my acceptance does not merge into yours), run_tests on your final exact version, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and submit_integration. If you change anything after this, it is a new candidate and needs another review.
